name: BEACON
description: Capture live evidence before changing a system.
example: Survey services, network settings, or authentication state before repair.

name: VESSEL
description: A structured container for moving meaningful state between environments, sessions, or tools.
example: Package an investigation handoff for another working environment.

name: BELT
description: A clipboard-oriented way to transport a prepared Vessel.
example: Copy a hydrated handoff to another console or conversation.

name: FOUNDRY
description: Convert observations into useful procedures, scripts, notes, and other artifacts.
example: Turn a completed troubleshooting session into an SOP.

name: VERIFY
description: Compare observed results against intended state after an operation.
example: Confirm a repaired service is running and a changed file has the expected hash.

name: ORCHARD
description: Preserve living tools, scripts, surveys, templates, and known-good techniques for reuse.
example: Plant a successful site-survey technique for the next visit.

name: MUSEUM
description: Record investigation history, evidence, discoveries, decisions, and lineage.
example: Archive what happened and why a repair was chosen.

name: ADAPTER
description: Translate external tool-specific interfaces into common states and capabilities.
example: Give several management portals a consistent readiness display.

name: PORTAL POWER
description: Show which authenticated management environments are available or degraded.
example: Distinguish READY from AUTH REQUIRED or DEGRADED.

name: WORKSHOP
description: House repeatable utilities that perform defined operations.
example: Run a known-good local validation or transformation.

name: LIBRARY
description: Find preserved context and artifacts from previous work.
example: Recover a documented repair before repeating it.

name: SPACE ROCK
description: Mark anomalies, blockers, and important findings during an investigation.
example: Preserve an unexpected dependency without losing the investigation thread.

name: SURVEY
description: Observe a system and collect evidence about its current state without intentionally modifying it.
example: Inspect services, disk health, network settings, and logs before attempting a repair.

name: SRBF METHOD
description: A four-stage workflow: survey the current state, reason from the evidence, bake a controlled change, and fossilize the verified result.
example: Survey an application, reason through a repair, bake the patch, then fossilize its validated state.

name: FOSSIL
description: Record a completed and validated implementation so its evidence, decisions, and recovery context remain available.
example: Preserve a successful build, its validation results, backup location, and release notes.

name: FMI
description: A safety principle for RSI-driven development. Each ring surveys the current application, compares it against defined acceptance criteria, skips completed work, applies only necessary changes, and validates the result. Iteration stops when all required criteria are satisfied.
example: RSI builds an app through successive rings: inspect the current implementation, identify the next unmet requirement, make a bounded change, run validation, and repeat only while requirements remain unmet. Re-running a completed ring should leave the verified state unchanged.
